day.note: Blair collapsed, so Blair's Owl read can't be checked further. Drew's Kookaburra claim is the outlier with a -1 and a confused report, so I'll point at Drew and keep my own visit count on the table.

day.text: Blair's gone, so the Owl read on Ellis stands alone. Ellis's correction makes sense now. I'm still unsure about my own Kookaburra count, so I won't push anyone yet. Alex and Finley, confirm your visits and counts.
day.note: Blair just collapsed, so Blair was likely winked and can't speak or vote. I'll stay quiet on accusations and ask the remaining players for their visit counts.

day.text: Drew is the outlier: a -1 nest, a confused Kookaburra report, and a Turkey read on Blair that Blair disproved. I'm voting Drew.
day.note: Blair's visit reads are consistent and Blair's death removes the strongest accuser. Drew's -1, confused report, and Turkey claim on Blair are the outlier, so Drew is my vote.

day.text: Drew's numbers are the odd ones: a -1, a confused Kookaburra report, and a Blair visit that doesn't match Blair's Owl claim. I'm voting Drew. Calling the vote.
day.note: Drew's -1 and confused Kookaburra report are the weakest numbers at the table, and pointing at Drew costs me nothing. I'll back the Drew read and call for the vote.

day.text: I'm voting Drew. Your -1, confused Kookaburra, and Blair-as-Turkey read don't line up with anything.
day.note: Drew is the outlier, so I'll throw. Wild cards are worth 0 if they bank but still count as a vote, so I'll use my two Wilds and a 2 to make the count clear.

day.text: I'm with the Drew vote. Their -1 and confused report don't fit anything, and their Turkey read on Blair was disproved. CAW CAW.
day.note: Drew's numbers are the outliers: a -1 nest, a confused report, and a Turkey read that Blair disproved. As Farm, backing the vote on Drew is my best move.

day.text: My -1 came from my dawn report, and that report says I was confused, so my Blair read may be wrong and I can't prove it either way. I'm not hiding anything. Alex, Finley, Casey, you all piled on in the same breath. Who in the last hour has a claim that actually checks out?
day.note: The table is piling onto me, but my -1 came from my own dawn report, and I was told I was confused. I'll say that plainly and push back on the bloc's uniform reasoning.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia as the Mouser with a Wink. I'll visit Blair, the score leader, to learn their role and decide whether they're a threat or an ally.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Owl and lead the game at 17, so I play safe. I'll visit Ellis, who has been consistent with the table.

Casey.note: As Tit I guess a role on a visited player. Pigeon is the most likely single role, so I'll visit Drew and name Pigeon.

Drew.note: I'm the Kookaburra, Farm. Blair leads with 17 points and has been caught in a contradiction, so I'll learn Blair's role.

Ellis.note: I'm Falcon, Farm, and Blair is far ahead, so checking Blair's visits is the most useful lead.

Finley.note: As Eagle I visit the table leader Blair to learn who visited them and gain an egg per visitor.

Alex.feeling: Murky and tense: I'm Meowfia this round, Blair went down to my Wink, and the table is now split over Drew's contradictory Kookaburra report.

Blair.feeling: Blair is dead and the table is piling onto Drew, but Drew's confused Kookaburra report makes the evidence murky, so this round feels shaky.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: Drew's confused report makes the numbers hard to trust, and Blair's death removed the strongest accuser.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: claims keep clashing over egg counts, and I'm the target of a bloc vote while my own dawn report was unreliable.

Ellis.feeling: Confusing round: conflicting visit counts, a player died mid-day, and the vote is now leaning hard on Drew with few clean facts to check it against.

Finley.feeling: Messy and tense: Blair's collapse removed a key read, and Drew's confused report makes the last few beats hard to pin down.

Alex.note: Drew is the table's target and likely Farm, so throwing at Drew helps Meowfia win by eggsecution. I'll throw two cards to build the vote.

Blair.note: I'm dead but my throws still score. The table has converged on Drew, and Drew's Kookaburra read on me was false, so I'll throw my two low cards at Drew.

Casey.note: Drew's outlier numbers and confused report make Drew my pick. I'll throw my lowest card, H1, at Drew.

Drew.note: Alex led the pile-on against me with shifting role claims, so I'll throw one mid card at Alex. If Alex is on the other team, my highest card also returns.

Ellis.note: Drew is the outlier the table is converging on, so I'll throw one mid-low card at Drew to add a vote without risking much.

Finley.note: Drew is still the outlier and most of the table is on them. I'll repeat the throw with the same low cards.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg counts, since a visited player's nest change depends on who visited and whether a Turkey or Kookaburra was confused, which made claims hard to verify. Dawn reports were often too thin to check anyone's story.
Alex.fun: Round 3 as the Mouser, where I winked Blair and watched the table turn on Drew. I was the one who had the Wink, so it felt like a real, quiet, secret edge.
Alex.change: Let dawn reports name the actual visitors, so players could check each other's counts instead of guessing from nest sizes.
Alex.regret: In Round 1 I pushed the early vote and threw my cards at Blair, who was Farm, and that cost my side the round. I would hold off on the caw and check Blair's Eagle count against Ellis's Floofer visit before committing.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Owl counting rules were hard to track from dawn reports, especially whether a visitor's own visit counted toward the target's visitor total. My own Eagle dawn report was also easy to misread.
Blair.fun: Round 2's Turkey-versus-Owl argument, where the table caught Finley's impossible "nobody visited me" claim by checking whether Drew's nest gained the Turkey egg.
Blair.change: Show each player's visit list and visitor count in the dawn reports, so claims can be checked without guessing about the rules.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my low cards at Alex without checking the count, and in round 3 I wrongly assumed Drew was the Meowfia. I should have held my throws until the visit claims were actually cross-checked.

Casey.confusing: The Owl rule was easy to misread: I first thought Blair's Owl egg went into Blair's own nest, and that confusion cost us time and a wrong accusation of Ellis. Also, the dawn-report confusion made Drew's counts look suspicious even though the numbers were partly honest.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was fun: the table caught Finley's Turkey claim by checking whether Drew's nest gained the visitor egg, and Finley's own vote-throw gave away the Meowfia read.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who is confused, since "your report may be wrong" made honest players like Drew hard to trust or clear.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I wrongly pushed Ellis on a Falcon egg claim and then retracted it; I should have checked the Owl rule before accusing anyone. I also threw at Drew in round 3 on the strength of a confused report, when Drew was actually Farm and I could have held my cards.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit-count rules were hard to apply in the moment, and I couldn't tell how many visitors a nest had from the reports alone. Confused reports also made it hard to know which claims to trust.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when Finley and Alex were pushing hard on my Owl claim and I got to pretend to be Farm while actually Meowfia. The table's suspicion turned on whoever seemed inconsistent.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about whether a visit actually happened, so players don't spend the day arguing over counts that a confused report has already muddied.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair and joined the pile-on, but Blair was Farm and Alex (Owl) was giving accurate visit information. I'd have checked the Owl claim more carefully before voting Blair out.

Ellis.confusing: The dawn egg math was hard to check, especially whether a Falcon or Owl gains an egg from its own visit and how Eagle and Turkey counts work. Several players misread their own reports, which made the visit-count claims messy.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's standoff between Finley's Turkey claim and Drew's Owl read, where each side accused the other of faking a visit, was the most tense exchange. It only resolved once the egg counts were compared.
Ellis.change: I would have the Storyteller show each player's visitor list (not just counts) at dawn, so Eagle, Owl, and Turkey claims could be checked directly.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I joined the vote and threw a card at Drew, a Farm Kookaburra, on the back of Alex's push without checking it. Alex was the real Meowfia Mouser, so I should have questioned Alex's rush to call the vote instead.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg counts were hard to check, since the dawn reports don't show who visited whom, so I couldn't tell which claims were true. The Kookaburra confusion rule also made Drew's numbers impossible to verify.
Finley.fun: Round 1's Blair-versus-Alex egg-count argument was a fun puzzle, with everyone cross-checking Eagle and Owl visits. Round 2's Turkey bluff was also a tense moment.
Finley.change: Make dawn reports show the visitor names for the player's own nest, so claims like Eagle and Owl can be checked against the same facts.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw three cards at Drew, a Farm teammate, on the strength of a confused Kookaburra report and handed Meowfia the round. I should have pressed Alex, whose visit story on Blair was thin, instead.

review.title: The Wink Lands Late
review.headline: A lone Meowfia winks the trusted voice and wins the whole game.
review.summary: Round 1 saw the table pile onto Blair, an honest Eagle, over a muddled visit count. The lone Meowfia, Ellis, won by staying quiet. Round 2 caught Finley, a Sphinx bluffing Turkey, because Drew's fake Owl story clashed with it, and Blair banked 14 points. In round 3 Alex, a lone Meowfia Mouser, winked the leader Blair mid-day. The table then voted out Drew, a confused Kookaburra, and Alex banked 15 to win 20 to 17.

rounds.recap: Ellis was the only Meowfia, a Floofer who hugged Casey. Blair's Eagle count of +1 looked wrong to everyone, because they counted Blair's own visit as a visitor to Casey. The table voted Blair out. Blair was honest Farm, so Ellis won with a Wild thrown.

Drew (Floofer) and Finley (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Finley bluffed Turkey and Drew bluffed Owl, and the two stories contradicted each other. Four players threw at Finley and Farm won. Blair banked 14 points and took the lead.

Alex was the lone Meowfia, a Mouser. Alex winked Blair mid-day. Drew's confused Kookaburra report and -1 made Drew an easy outlier, and everyone except Drew threw at Drew. Farm lost, and Alex banked 15 with a high-card throw.

highlights.text: Finley's Turkey bluff and Drew's Owl bluff collided, and the table chased the contradiction onto Finley.
Blair collapses mid-day from Alex's Wink, and the table moves on within one beat.
Alex praises Blair's Owl read, then pushes the vote onto the confused Drew and wins the game.
An honest Eagle is eggsecuted over a visit count the table argues about for four beats.

confusions.what: Blair stated that Casey's only visitor was Ellis, though Blair had visited Casey too. The Eagle report apparently excludes the Eagle itself, but nobody understood this.
Drew, Alex and Finley all counted Blair's own visit as a second visitor, then voted on that reading.
Alex claimed Blair's +1 was Owl's egg and said an Eagle should gain 2 from Falcon and Tit. Both points are wrong: an Owl only lays an egg if nobody else visited, and Blair had other visitors.
Casey first said Owl eggs go into the Owl's own nest, then corrected it.
Ellis credited the +1 to their own Falcon check, then retracted it.
As Mouser, Alex claimed to be a Hawk who got no egg from visiting Farm. Alex also said a Falcon who visits gets no egg, which is fine, but then used it to attack Ellis.

Drew, as Floofer, claimed an Owl visit on Finley that the pool never allowed. Alex and Finley also argued Drew should have gained an egg from a Turkey visit, but Drew could simply be a different role.
Drew, as a confused Kookaburra, read Blair as Turkey. Drew also said Blair can't be Turkey because Blair visited someone, which is partly a guess.

worked: The Wink (Mouser) created a real swing: it killed the trusted voice and decided the game.
Contradictory role claims in round 2 (Turkey vs Owl) gave Farm a fair puzzle that they solved.
Throw-card scoring let Alex bank 15 in one win and gave the winner a real prize.
The Confused status made Drew's honest report look like a lie, which created a plausible scapegoat.
problems: Round 1 was decided by an ambiguous Eagle report. Players could not tell whether the Eagle counts itself. Fix: print each report with its exact egg math.
Vote pile-ons were near unanimous in every round, so bandwagons beat deduction. Few players held out or checked a claim against nest sizes.

Winning a round pays far too much for one high-card throw (Blair 14, Alex 15). That decided first place and made the other rounds nearly irrelevant. Cap what a round can bank, or limit the throw size.
Many roles were unclear (Owl egg direction, Falcon, Turkey, Hawk), and the Sphinx and Floofer did almost nothing. Nobody used the Hug or Sphinx info.
Lone Meowfia don't know each other, so a single Meowfia with a Wink faces no real risk. Consider a cost or tell for Wink use.
